scope: Proposition 11.1 (Finite measure for equal labels) of the manuscript “Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations” (preprints/Localization-costs-and-information-growth-for-exact-Gaussian-observations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f43e1443f9fd513), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let r ≥ 1, p ≥ 2, and r + p − 1 ≤ d − 2. For every nonnegative Borel H, Z γr(dX) Z Rr ρ0,r(X, y)p Z H(X, y, s) µ⊗p X,y(ds) dy = (2π)−r(p−1)/2 Z J(s)−r µ⊗p (ds) Z H(X, Xs1, s) γr,Bs (dX). (173) These are finite measures before inserting H. They are supported on Xs1 = · · · = Xsp = y, full ranks of X and Bs, and positive-radius spherical fibers. The input uses the exact density and fiber versions above; its ball-average and Gaussian approximation versions agree at the constrained label outside a null set for the finite measure. The more general theorem permits bounded nonnegative densities over spherical or Gaussian base probability. Only the density-one spherical instance is used below.
